result.note: Tested the final US anti-dumping and countervailing duties on Indian solar products, India's EU steel quota and the carbon-levy catch, and the venue of Xi's first India visit since 2019.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about steel under the pending India–EU trade deal, as reported in September 2026:
items: India's steel exports to the EU will be exempt from the EU's carbon levy as soon as the deal takes effect.
India secured annual access of about 1.64 million tonnes of steel to the EU.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the separate EU carbon levy stays in place until Brussels recognises India's carbon-credit scheme. The quota access matters because Europe's new July steel regime reserves half its import quota for free-trade partners and hits the rest with a 50% duty.
questions.source: The catch is the separate EU carbon levy, which stays in place until Brussels recognises India's carbon-credit scheme, the same fight India is running with the UK.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about US trade action on Indian solar products in September 2026:
items: The US Commerce Department finalised an anti-dumping margin of more than 120% on Indian solar cells and panels.
The United States bought more than 95% of India's solar exports when the preliminary rate was announced.
A US trade commission vote in October 2026 is the last step before duty orders are issued.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The final anti-dumping margin was 123.04%, alongside a 126.09% countervailing duty, and the trade commission vote on October 14 is the last gate before duty orders in November. India's own solar-localisation rules leave domestic projects to absorb output the factories can no longer sell abroad.
questions.source: The United States bought more than 95% of India's solar exports when the preliminary rate landed, and a US trade commission vote on October 14 is the last gate before duty orders in November.

questions.prompt: In September 2026, Chinese President Xi Jinping made his first visit to India since 2019. Which summit in Delhi did he attend?
questions.explain: Modi and Xi met on the sidelines of the Delhi BRICS summit, where Modi held that border peace remains the precondition for normal ties. Xi pushed a "Greater BRICS" integrated market and a China-led AI zone.
questions.source: Modi and Xi met on the sidelines of the Delhi BRICS summit, Xi's first India visit since 2019, with Modi holding that border peace remains the precondition for normal ties.
